title: responses compatibility: feature matrix, prioritized parity gaps, and experimental fallback designs
creator: Ana Delgado
description:
Summary: We need a concise feature-level mapping between the OpenAI Responses API and Redwood's Responses model and runtime behavior, produce a prioritized list of parity gaps that materially affect customer migrations, and design a set of experimental fallbacks that minimize customer-visible regressions while we implement full parity. This ticket covers discovery, matrix creation, early PoC fallback designs, and the test plan for behavioral validation.

Background: Several customers are asking to migrate workloads that depend on the OpenAI Responses contract (streaming events, tool/function calling semantics, structured output enforcement, response metadata, content safety signaling). Previously created artifacts focus on adapters and runtime shims, but we lack a compact, prioritized feature matrix with reproducible test cases and small fallback mechanisms we can prototype in-hours. This ticket complements the broader adapter work by making trade-offs explicit and providing short-lived remediations for high-impact gaps.

Goals: (1) Produce a feature matrix contrasting OpenAI Responses fields/behaviors with Redwood Responses and runtime edge cases (streaming chunking, event ordering, partial tool call emission), (2) Identify and prioritize parity gaps based on customer impact and implementation cost, (3) Design 2-3 experimental fallbacks we can ship to hosted API and Redwood Dedicated as feature flags for canary customers, (4) Define an automated behavioral test harness and a small evaluation prompt corpus to quantify regressions.

Scope / non-goals: We are not implementing a full backwards-compatible gateway in this ticket. Full adapter rollout and backward-compatible SDKs are separate follow-ups. This ticket should yield a concrete matrix, prioritized list, one or two small PoC fallbacks (e.g., event buffering with reorder heuristics, best-effort tool-name normalization, structured-output post-processor), and an eval harness with initial test cases.

Key compatibility vectors to analyze: streaming token/event model differences; tool/function calling (name matching, partial arg streaming, tool-result objects); structured output vs unstructured completions (JSON coercion, validators, best-effort repair); stop sequence/termination behavior; presence/absence of top-level metadata (safety labels, model-internal reasons, warnings); multistream boundaries for multi-response documents; delta in function-calling error semantics; idempotency and request-level identifiers; content-length/fragmentation assumptions customers rely on.

Deliverables: 
- responses-compatibility-feature-matrix.md (human readable) summarizing each field/behavior and compatibility status (Full | Partial | Missing | Behavioral-delta).
- prioritized_parity_gaps.csv (compact list with severity, estimated effort, proposed mitigation).
- two experimental fallback designs (docs + minimal config hooks): streaming-event-buffering and function-call-name-relaxation + post-call-reconciliation.
- evaluation harness: small test corpus (10-15 prompts) and a harness runner that records diffs between OpenAI baseline and Redwood output (stored artifacts links in attachments).

Trade-offs and constraints: 
- Strict fidelity vs latency: buffering to emulate exact OpenAI event ordering can add tens to hundreds of ms. We must bound latency increase per customer tier. Fallbacks should be toggled per-customer.
- Semantic repair vs hallucination risk: structured-output post-processing can force syntactic correctness but risks masking underlying model regressions. For high-sensitivity customers, we should prefer warnings and suggestion metadata instead of automatic rewriting.
- Operational complexity: every fallback increases runtime variance and testing surface. Limit initial fallbacks to designs that are reversible and observable.

Acceptance criteria (minimum): 
- Completed feature matrix that covers at least 28 API behaviors/fields and clearly marks parity status.
- A prioritized list of the top 8 parity gaps with rationale and rough engineering estimates (S/M/L).
- Two fallback designs documented with configuration knobs, expected latency impact estimate, and runbook for enabling/disabling per-tenant.
- An evaluation harness with 10 canonical prompts and automation that produces a diff report between Redwood baseline and an OpenAI Responses reference.
- A short implementation plan and canary rollout checklist for the highest-priority fallback.

Risks: 
- Customers may rely on undocumented OpenAI behaviors. We must flag any undocumented behaviors and recommend conservative opt-in.
- Fallbacks may create subtle data divergence that affects logs/metrics and billing. Include telemetry instrumentation recommendations.

Links and references: 
- Existing adapters audit: https://confluence.redwood.ai/responses-adapter-audit (internal)
- Runtime fallback research notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/fallbacks/research.pdf
- Prior evaluation harness: GH PR #1142 - responses-diff-harness (link in attachments)

Notes for implementers: Attach all diff artifacts produced by the harness to the PRs. Keep fallbacks behind feature flags and include a telemetry ping describing discrepancy reasons (e.g., "event-order-repaired", "func-name-relaxed", "structured-output-fixed").

comments: 2026-03-10 Ana Delgado: Created initial ticket after sync with PM and runtime leads. Prioritized streaming and function-calling as first vectors.
2026-03-11 Kunal Mehta: Ran quick scan against current runtime. Observed: Redwood streams token fragments differently when tool-call events interleave; will capture sample traces and attach.

2026-03-12 Priya Raman (PM): Added customer examples where function-call partial args were relied upon by orchestration layer; flagged high customer impact for function-call arg streaming differences.
2026-03-12 Design review (@Leah Kim): Suggested UX requirements for opt-in fallback toggles and clear telemetry labels for any automatic fixes.
2026-03-13 Kunal Mehta: Uploaded preliminary event traces and a small script that simulates OpenAI event ordering. Next: produce the feature-matrix stub and run the harness against 5 prompts.
2026-03-13 Engineering note: Keep experimental fallbacks as per-tenant feature flags. Avoid automatic on-by-default fixes for enterprise customers until telemetry is evaluated.
